newsitem.title: UK: Colombia to reopen May/June coffee registrations.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to reopen May/June coffee registrations.

text.p: Colombia's National Coffee Growers' confirmed on Monday it would reopen May/June coffee registrations for shipment of a maximum 500,000 60 kg bags by private exporters to Europe and Japan.

Speaking to reporters at a London meeting of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC), Jorge Cardenas said there would be no change to the volumes which the Federation had already committed to buyers.

"The quantity of coffee committed by the Federation will be passed to private exporters. The amount is up to 500,000 bags for May and June shipments and the coffee will go to Europe and Japan," Cardenas said.
Last week Cardenas was quoted as saying the federation was having difficulties meeting its export commitments because of an unusually tight supply of coffee on the domestic market.
Asked on Monday why the Federation has decided to take the move, Cardenas replied: "The exporters pay higher prices than the federation internally to the farmers."
"The Federation is under no condition to buy the coffee from them," he said.
Registrations for shipments by private exporters in April, May and June were originally opened by the Federation on March 7 and industry sources said they were shut down suddenly on April 14.
